newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's gold trade plunges in July on crackdown.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's gold trade plunges in July on crackdown.

text.p: South Korea's gold imports and exports plunged in July following a government crackdown on the booming bullion transshipment trade, trade ministry statistics obtained on Wednesday showed.

Imports in July plunged 49.6 percent to $335 million from $665 million a month ago and $255 million a year earlier. Exports tumbled 50.9 percent to $318 million from $648 million in June and $234 in July last year.
The crackdown on the speculative transshipment business began on July 1.

Bullion houses were importing huge amounts of gold on 90-day deferred payment, immediately exporting the metal and parking the proceeds in high interest-bearing money market instruments. They reaped huge profits from arbitrage between domestic and overseas interest rates.
Traders said all major Korean bullion houses had slashed their operations since the government shortened the deferred payment period to a maximum 30 days.
A sliding Korean won also dampened the business.

"For 30 days deferred payment, nobody wants to do business," said a trader with Ssangyong Corp, who declined to be named. He said he believed the September gold trade figures would show further declines after contracts in the pipeline before the crackdown had been fulfilled.
